Delivery & Returns

التوصيل والإرجاع

Draft awaiting review by a UAE lawyer. It describes how lili works today; the Arabic version will be the one that counts once it is published.

The ways a seller can get a piece to you in the UAE and the GCC, who pays for delivery, and what to do if it doesn't arrive or isn't as described.

How a piece gets to you

Each listing shows the couriers that seller is happy to send the piece with, chosen by her when she listed it:

  • Aramex: within the UAE and to the rest of the GCC.
  • Emirates Post: within the UAE.
  • Quiqup same-day: within the UAE.
  • SMSA Express: within the UAE and to the rest of the GCC.
  • DHL Express: within the UAE and to the rest of the GCC.

lili does not deliver anything and has no account with any courier. The seller books the courier herself and gives you the courier's tracking number.

Where delivery is offered

Inside the UAE, and to Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain and Oman. Outside the UAE you may owe customs duty or VAT when the parcel arrives, and some materials (exotic skins, ivory, some perfumes) can't cross borders. The seller checks with her courier before she sends.

Delivery fees

The seller picks a parcel size from extra small to extra large, and the listing shows each courier's fee for that size. Fees marked “estimated” are lili's estimate of the courier's public price, not a quote: the courier's own price on the day is the one that counts. Unless you and the seller agree otherwise, the buyer pays the delivery fee.

A seller who switches on bundling lets you buy several of her pieces together and pay one delivery fee for the largest parcel.

Paying for a delivered piece

lili takes no payment, so with courier delivery you and the seller agree how you pay. Paying before the parcel arrives means trusting someone you haven't met: lili cannot refund it. Prefer cash on delivery where the courier offers it, ask for a video of the piece first, and look at the shop's reviews.

If it doesn't arrive, or isn't as described

  • Message the seller in lili first, with photos. Most problems are a misunderstanding about condition or size.
  • If the parcel is lost or damaged in transit, the seller claims from the courier using the tracking number.
  • If the seller won't help, report the shop in lili. We read the listing and your messages, and can remove the listing and close the shop. We tell you what we decided and why.

Returns

A private seller doesn't have to take back a piece that is as described. If a piece isn't as described or isn't genuine, ask the seller to take it back and refund you, and report the shop if she won't. A business seller must also give you the return and refund rights UAE consumer protection law requires.
